html:
Part B — pipeline, operations and documentation review

The saved artifacts establish three valid scenarios and working offline grading of the tracked example, but they do not establish all of the pipeline's stronger guarantees. The reviewed snapshot had two P1 issues: interactive trials changed identity after Temporal planned their unit, and repeated withholding selections could remove requirements without recording their full text. A late check found that a concurrent change fixed the scaffold identity mismatch; the withholding issue remains. Other material gaps affect probe reuse, control quality, build identity, scaffold separation, the console's disclosure/confirmation gates, and the interpretation of recorded measurements. The reports should not be used to claim a measured interaction benefit or complete reproducibility of the current pipeline.

This report is independent of Part A. Source citations point to the frozen review copy at /private/tmp/swesim-independent-review/snapshot/, captured at HEAD a76654a5943f702ecb99ae6eb4413a4f8287da15 with then-current working edits to orchestration/tests. The original checkout changed concurrently. No repository files were modified, and no cloud jobs were started by this review. Four small local checks used repository functions with synthetic inputs or read-only artifacts; their results are in local-repros.json. The console was started locally and queried; invalid POST bodies were used to avoid any mutation or workflow launch.

Late concurrent-change check: after the snapshot, the working checkout at HEAD 15bf683a05ec added a shared scaffold_identity helper to planning and execution. A read-only calculation now gives identical planned/effective IDs (ab386aa941387001a200908e) for the then-current seaborn interactive build. B-P1-1's specific scaffold defect is therefore fixed in that later code, while the snapshot finding and original reproduction are retained for audit. No cloud run or full post-change test suite was performed. The withholding change was only a zero-selection retry/nudge and does not fix B-P1-2. See late-check evidence and later source. The rest of this report is a snapshot review, not a complete review of that later checkout.

Findings, ranked

B-P1-1 — Planned interactive trial identity differs from executed identity. Status: fixed in the late concurrent-change check. plan_trials constructs RunConfig without agent_config and derives the workflow/unit ID. execute_trial_request verifies that identity, then calls run_trial, which adds the compiled scaffold hash and recomputes the ID. The actual record.json is consequently written under another trial directory, while await_trial_activity polls the originally planned one. The unit can finish successfully but appear unresolved. Established at swesim/workflows/activities.py:527, swesim/workflows/activities.py:795, swesim/stages/run.py:87, swesim/workflows/activities.py:744. The read-only check on the saved seaborn build produced planned ID bc77a468bcf9653e891663da and effective ID dcef3ea9ef0798c13f94845e. Existing run-stage scaffold coverage does not cover this integration: tests/test_run.py:294, tests/test_workflows.py:549. Smallest fix: one shared effective-config function used before planning and before execution, including scaffold/profile/build; reject drift rather than silently re-identifying a planned trial. Assert that the returned record ID equals the request/unit ID. This also applies when a build changes between planning and execution.

B-P1-2 — A repeated selected phrase can silently remove a different requirement. withhold expands every matching occurrence to sentence boundaries, but stores only the first expanded sentence as the ledger excerpt. Other expanded sentences can contain additional requirements. Reproduction: selecting “Expected values are numeric” from two sentences ending “when option enabled” and “and preserve all nulls” deletes both, yet records only the first sentence. _integrity only checks that the recorded excerpt existed, disappeared, and the title survived; it does not prove that all other text survived. Established at swesim/stages/draft_spec.py:308, swesim/stages/draft_spec.py:322, swesim/stages/draft_spec.py:331, swesim/stages/draft_spec.py:1315, swesim/models.py:142; the current repeated-occurrence test is tests/test_swebench_source.py:834. Consequence: an agent can lose a requirement the stakeholder ledger also fails to preserve. Smallest fix: record each distinct expanded occurrence verbatim, then verify the withheld brief against an exact reconstruction from all recorded deletion ranges.

There is a separate grounding limit under the same task-fidelity contract: arbitrary model-authored requirement text can have fact_id=None and is copied directly into the spec. Fact grounding proves that an excerpt occurs in a corpus; it does not prove the fact text means the same thing, and requirements need no independent ledger entry. See swesim/models.py:77, swesim/models.py:166, swesim/stages/draft_spec.py:409, swesim/stages/draft_spec.py:1283. Require grounded provenance for every requirement and an explicit operation for any deliberate task change. Code-generated natural/withheld brief construction does correctly prevent the model from directly replacing either brief with arbitrary prose.

B-P2-1 — A new probe binding can be attached to old cached execution. The direct reuse checks compare probe.binding with the current row, but probe_tests always names its Harbor job by instance ID. harbor_cli.run_task returns the one existing terminal trial without comparing its inputs. _probe_record then computes a fresh binding from the current row. Therefore changing base_commit or test_patch and requesting a new probe can reuse old statuses and label them with the new hash. Established by swesim/sources/github_repo.py:438, swesim/sources/github_repo.py:474, swesim/sources/github_repo.py:382, swesim/harbor_cli.py:44. reconstruct_probe similarly has no original input binding to check for legacy unbound evidence. Consequence: “bound measurement” is weaker than advertised; later validation may catch it, after spending a draft/build. Smallest fix: bind job directories and persisted probe inputs to base, test patch, gold patch, image/interpreter and runner version, and verify those recorded inputs before reuse.

The faithful-command guarantee is also incomplete: absent exact stages are accepted, explicitly skipped measurements can be reused, and the final subset is not remeasured after order-dependent IDs are dropped. The probe executes as root (test_user=None), whereas grading executes as tester. See swesim/sources/github_repo.py:262, swesim/sources/github_repo.py:348, swesim/stages/mine.py:99, swesim/stages/draft_spec.py:1139. Require completed exact stages on the final retained set, under the grading identity/environment, and reject unverifiable legacy reuse. The final no-op/oracle sweep is a useful backstop, not evidence that the earlier probe was faithful.

B-P2-2 — The fallback wrong control can retain exactly the gold behavior. The lexical mask starts with no open string at each diff hunk. A hunk beginning inside an existing multiline docstring is thus treated as executable code. In a local check, the fallback inverted a Boolean inside that docstring, retained the gold code fix, passed git apply --check, and had the same executable AST as gold. Established at swesim/stages/draft_spec.py:961, swesim/stages/draft_spec.py:985, swesim/stages/draft_spec.py:1023. Current coverage handles strings/comments whose delimiters are available in the hunk: tests/test_swebench_source.py:1198. A model-authored control is also never compared for semantic equivalence with gold; it is checked for application only. Consequence: the draft can claim a meaningful negative control that is actually correct; the final sweep should reject it, producing avoidable candidate failures. Smallest fix: reconstruct complete files, tokenize/parse from the file beginning, reject docstring/comment-only or unchanged executable AST mutations, and retain behavioral validation as the final authority. Static syntax changes alone cannot prove semantic incorrectness.

Verification booleans generally record actual apply results, including None when git is absent. However, control_notes.clear() discards earlier correction-round results, so metadata is not a chronological audit. The fallback also accepts None from an unfetched-file verification, unlike the stricter model-control path. See swesim/stages/draft_spec.py:834, swesim/stages/draft_spec.py:1036, swesim/stages/draft_spec.py:1226, swesim/stages/draft_spec.py:1241. Preserve an append-only attempt log and reject unfetched: for fallback controls too.

B-P2-3 — compiled_hash does not cover every input to the rendered task. It hashes spec, base digest, agent version, templates, verifier and shims. It does not hash compiler logic/constants or several render inputs such as stakeholder URL, allowed hosts, timeout and review configuration. The same hash can consequently identify different rendered tasks; changing compiler-owned policy/configuration also need not change it. The run stage does not verify a manifest of compiled output files before consuming them. Established at swesim/stages/compile.py:198, swesim/stages/compile.py:252, swesim/stages/compile.py:217, swesim/stages/run.py:64, swesim/stages/run.py:82. Consequence: build-validation reuse and lineage can overstate what was validated. Smallest fix: hash a canonical manifest of rendered non-secret task inputs, including compiler-owned configuration; check it before materialization. The token must remain a per-trial input outside the shared build hash. Templates, all rendered brief profiles and the scaffold are now generated at compile time, which is a real improvement.

B-P2-4 — The base manifests are written but never compared or checked. Both Dockerfiles generate /opt/swesim/base-manifest.txt; no collector, grader, validation or run code consumes it. A repository-wide search finds only the two writers and a test checking ordering of Dockerfile strings. Pipelines also mask upstream command failures unless each stage's status is checked. Established at swesim/templates/environment.Dockerfile.j2:13, swesim/templates/tests.Dockerfile.j2:11, tests/test_compile.py:482. Consequence: the manifest does not fail closed when agent and verifier base contents differ. This matters because the images independently execute mutable installation steps. Smallest fix: export the agent's trusted pre-submission base manifest, compare it to the verifier's before applying changes, and explicitly fail on manifest-generation errors. Pin built image digests or package inputs where reproducibility is claimed. The HEAD assertion and populated-submodule guards are useful separate checks.

B-P2-5 — Legacy scaffold and non-scaffold trials still pool. The saved seaborn group interactive|withheld|6fb358… includes attempts 20/21 without the scaffold and 50/51 with it. Both older run_config.json files omit the new field, while the latter reports contain agent_config_sha256=02791a33…. group_key trusts the existing hash and summarize checks model/purpose, not the actual scaffold. Established at swesim/stages/score.py:256, swesim/stages/score.py:324, workspace/scenarios/mwaskom--seaborn-3190/scores.json:198, workspace/trials/c39a73b6cfdffdc66581af1a/report.json:572. Consequence: an n=4 group reports pass@3/pass^3=1 even though separating the two treatments gives n=2 each and therefore null at k=3. Smallest fix: split historical scoring groups using the recorded scaffold digest and flag missing lineage, without rewriting immutable original trial IDs. New RunConfig.agent_config hashes distinguish new runs, but do not repair existing records.

B-P2-6 — The console does not fully enforce its evaluator gate. _public_rows strips the older audit keys but leaves new redacted_terms and withheld_sentences, exposing the very sentences removed from v2 replies through the default timeline API. A local synthetic check confirms this. In addition, raw judge.json and draft.meta.json are served without ?evaluator=1; they contain test-derived evidence. Established at swesim/dashboard/app.py:84, swesim/dashboard/app.py:277, swesim/dashboard/render.py:20, swesim/dashboard/app.py:244. Live localhost GETs returned 200 for those files, while scenario.json and transcript.json correctly returned 403. Consequence: selecting the normal view does not exclude evaluator information. Smallest fix: build public responses from a whitelist, include the new audit fields in the evaluator-only data, and gate artifacts containing raw judge/test evidence. The console is an operator surface, not directly exposed to the sandbox agent; that limits the impact but does not satisfy B8.

B-P2-7 — Create/run are immediate actions, and origin checking is hostname-only. The create/run form sends its first submit straight to the API; validation has no confirmation requirement. Label/review writes likewise lack a separate confirmation step; cancellation is the exception. same_origin accepts a missing Origin and compares only hostnames, ignoring scheme/port. Established by swesim/dashboard/static/app.js:199, swesim/dashboard/console.py:111, swesim/dashboard/app.py:328, swesim/dashboard/app.py:71. With a deliberately invalid body, a request from http://127.0.0.1:9876 reached validation (400), whereas an unrelated hostname and Origin: null were rejected (403). Tests explicitly permit another port and absent Origin: tests/test_dashboard.py:211. Consequence: accidental expensive starts are one click away, and “only from the console's own pages” is false. Smallest fix: a review/confirm step bound to canonical request content, exact origin validation and a console-issued CSRF token. No valid state-changing request was submitted during review.

B-P2-8 — Calibration arithmetic is correct, but the interpretation and saved evidence are insufficient. The confusion totals produce agreement 95/145=0.655172, precision 29/45=0.644444 and recall 29/63=0.460317. However, the positive prediction is verified_rubric_score >= 2, not accept()/keep. The docs describe these numbers as precision/recall “when it keeps a row.” Furthermore, the CLI removes per_instance before output, and the saved JSON/log contains only aggregates, so the confusion matrix cannot be independently reconstructed from saved predictions and human labels. Established at swesim/stages/judge.py:166, swesim/stages/judge.py:326, swesim/cli.py:169, workspace/judge_calibration.json:2, docs/grading.md:249. Smallest fix: label the metric as rubric-threshold agreement, separately compute acceptance precision/recall if desired, and persist all row IDs, predictions, labels and errors.

B-P2-9 — Several “current measured” claims are stale or unsupported. The frozen artifacts contain 28 local trials: 17 correct, 7 incorrect, 4 evaluator failures, plus three correct VM trials; 15 local interactive attempts reached the agent and four asked, making 4/17 when the two VM interactive attempts are included. README still says 25 local, 15/6/4, and 3/14. Nine noninteractive exports are training-eligible, contradicting the blanket “all episodes false” statement. The example has two runs and 102 manifest entries, and the registered seaborn build is cfa48d128c0f…, not the earlier build described as still registered. Established by artifact-summary.json, README.md:143, docs/grading.md:133, docs/grading.md:202. Smallest fix: generate tables from a frozen artifact inventory and give historical tables an explicit cutoff/build list.

The VM history establishes progress and a single launch across the worker change, but the saved evidence has no SSH connection/session log establishing the claimed absence of an SSH session/tunnel. assemble_ops.py sets laptop_off.passed=True from record existence, and the acceptance script checks the asserted flag and file existence, not the stated disconnection window. See workspace/evidence/assemble_ops.py:18, scripts/verify.sh:155, docs/ops.md:141. Preserve connection/session evidence or label this part operator-reported. The lid-open caveat is already stated honestly; this finding does not confuse disconnection with a closed lid.

B-P3-1 — The README's “offline suite” command requires an unlisted file. uv run --frozen --offline python -m pytest -q tests includes the explicit integration test, which reads os.environ['TEMPORAL_TEST_SERVER'] without a default. A stranger following the listed prerequisites has neither that variable nor its referenced cached server executable. Established at README.md:39, tests/integration/test_temporal.py:18. Smallest fix: add --ignore=tests/integration to the quick-start command, and document separate integration-server setup. I did not run the integration test, per the Part A execution restriction.

B1–B10 disposition

Area What is handled / what is not
B1 — measured F2P/P2P F2P is failed/error with the test patch on base and passed with gold; P2P is passed on both. Failed-on-both, regression and skip/xfail transitions are dropped. Exact-order differences are removed. The label network_or_env classifies a transition, not a demonstrated cause. Missing exact stages, final-subset replay, execution identity and cache input binding are incomplete; see B-P2-1. swesim/sources/github_repo.py:315, tests/test_github_repo.py:352, tests/test_github_repo.py:369
B1 — gold/protected overlap Direct gold paths are removed from proposed extras, and exact overlap with test files raises. This is string equality, not the grader's normalized glob matching; default protected files can also be gold-touched. Final oracle validation is the backstop. swesim/stages/draft_spec.py:706, swesim/verifier/policy.py:34
B2 — withholding Natural text comes from the row; model-provided briefs are ignored. Kept ranges preserve bytes, with line-aware whitespace removal. Title, normalized excerpt length (12 chars / 3 words), category and deletion fraction are checked. Repeated expanded occurrences and schema reconstruction are incomplete; B-P1-2. swesim/stages/draft_spec.py:189, swesim/stages/draft_spec.py:238, tests/test_swebench_source.py:703, tests/test_swebench_source.py:737
B2 — grounding Both sides strip leading blockquotes, collapse whitespace and casefold. Provenance selects the corpus; URLs need only be under the repository, not identify the exact comment/speaker. authored can use test/patch evidence. Fact-text entailment and independently grounded requirements are not enforced. swesim/stages/judge.py:70, swesim/stages/draft_spec.py:375, swesim/stages/draft_spec.py:409, tests/test_swebench_source.py:1569
B3 — judge Proposed gaps require nontrivial verbatim test/patch evidence; extracted gaps are recognized from actual extracted text, not a model source label. Thread resolution requires an excerpt; invalid resolution is downgraded. accept() then uses explicit booleans and resolution class. It does not itself repeat grounding. swesim/stages/judge.py:222, swesim/stages/judge.py:166, tests/test_swebench_source.py:399, tests/test_swebench_source.py:429
B3 — approval gate Asset and schema checks work. The “load-bearing interaction” gate is not a measurement: for a single F2P function, code links every unlinked on-request fact to it, then the gate checks only intersection. Arbitrary model-provided valid links are not substantively checked either. Keep this as a coverage annotation, or require evidence linking the fact to the asserted behavior. swesim/stages/draft_spec.py:763, swesim/stages/draft_spec.py:1084, swesim/stages/approve.py:31, tests/test_swebench_source.py:1352
B4 — controls Model files become difflib patches and are apply-checked; unchanged files and unfetched file keys are rejected. Only a confirmed missing base file becomes a new file. No-git is honestly unverified. Functional incorrectness is determined by the sweep, not proven at draft time; fallback and audit issues are B-P2-2. swesim/stages/draft_spec.py:806, swesim/stages/draft_spec.py:834, swesim/stages/draft_spec.py:866, swesim/sources/threads.py:75
B5 — launch/restart Intent before launch, persistent named user unit, one-attempt launch activity, read-only polling, and explicit unknown-state reconciliation are implemented. systemctl transport failure is not treated as absent unit. This is at-most-once with unresolved outcomes, not guaranteed eventual exactly-one launch. The snapshot had the scaffold identity defect in B-P1-1, fixed in the late check. swesim/workflows/activities.py:592, swesim/workflows/activities.py:610, swesim/workflows/activities.py:707, swesim/workflows/workflows.py:132, tests/test_workflows.py:339, tests/test_workflows.py:351
B5 — fan-out/approval Candidate IDs use ALLOW_DUPLICATE_FAILED_ONLY; terminal invalid/rejected children consume their IDs, while failed children may resume. max_parallel bounds whole candidate lifetimes, including held approval, not merely simultaneous validations. It is per workflow, not a global lock across batches. Signals are bound to spec hashes, and the approval activity rechecks disk. swesim/workflows/workflows.py:37, swesim/workflows/workflows.py:256, swesim/workflows/workflows.py:418, swesim/workflows/activities.py:436
B5 — credentials Unit commands contain a request path and non-secret environment paths. Provider/worker/GitHub secrets come from the ignored dotenv file. VM bootstrap sends an allowlisted key file; git authentication uses a transient helper, without embedding the token in the command. No secret-bearing workflow payload was identified in the saved histories inspected. Error scrubbing is not uniformly applied to all arbitrary exceptions. swesim/workflows/activities.py:663, swesim/workflows/activities.py:686, scripts/vm/create.sh:37, scripts/vm/setup.sh:97
B6 — images/network Tracked task: agent user agent, both baseline and phase allowlists; verifier separate and no-network; root collector, cleared environment, root-only artifact path. Session token is filled only for interactive. Test/oracle assets are copied to verifier/solution, not the ordinary agent context. build_context_assets can name arbitrary approved assets, however; schema/compiler do not forbid test/oracle assets there. swesim/templates/task.toml.j2:21, swesim/templates/task.toml.j2:35, swesim/stages/compile.py:253, swesim/stages/compile.py:272, tests/test_compile.py:202
B6 — hashes/base Templates, scaffold source and shims are hashed, and every brief profile is rendered at compile time. Render/config completeness and manifest enforcement are incomplete; B-P2-3/4. Declared empty submodule paths are allowed; populated/symlinked paths, parse failures and whitespace paths are rejected by the build guard. These do not compare the two base trees. swesim/stages/compile.py:47, swesim/stages/compile.py:262, tests/test_compile.py:465
B7 — scores Outcomes 1–4 enter n, 5–7 do not; unresolved attempts remain listed and uncounted; requested k is never reduced. Formula arithmetic agrees with records. New config hashes include scaffolds, but historical pooling remains; B-P2-5. swesim/stages/score.py:25, swesim/stages/score.py:160, swesim/stages/score.py:299
B7 — exports Reply observations are extracted from actual agent trajectory tool results; a generated service reply is not substituted. Ledger, assets and stakeholder audit are structurally under evaluator_only. Interactive eligibility requires a bound, adjudicated transcript; noninteractive episodes can legitimately be eligible. This does not certify the semantic cleanliness of text the policy actually received. swesim/stages/export.py:72, swesim/stages/export.py:114, tests/test_score.py:523, tests/test_score.py:652
B8 — console Text rendering escapes HTML and client updates use textContent; known-name artifact routes are enforced. Raw transcript/spec gating works. New audit fields, judge artifacts, confirmation and exact-origin requirements are incomplete; B-P2-6/7. No stored session token matched the sampled response bodies; that is not a proof that arbitrary artifact text can never contain a credential. swesim/dashboard/render.py:26, swesim/dashboard/static/app.js:10, swesim/dashboard/app.py:299, tests/test_dashboard.py:378
B9 — documentation Claim-by-claim disposition below. Code/artifact-backed claims are distinguished from historical summaries and unsupported causal/operational claims.
B10 — stranger Local review is possible from the tracked example. Creation and graded runs require the documented cloud/model credentials and a configured Temporal worker; they were not executed. The advertised offline test command has an additional undeclared server-file prerequisite; B-P3-1. Credential/dependency inventory follows.

One score table recomputed directly

For seaborn group interactive|withheld|6fb358…, the four records are 24ce7fb7…, 6e22b0ad…, c39a73b6…, and f88eb6db…. Every outcome is 1, every success is 1, and every reward is 1. Thus n=4, c=4, k=3:

Quantity Direct calculation Saved table
pass@3 1 − C(0,3)/C(4,3) = 1 1
pass^3 C(4,3)/C(4,3) = 1 1
mean reward (1+1+1+1)/4 = 1 1
infrastructure exclusions 0 0

The arithmetic matches workspace/scenarios/mwaskom--seaborn-3190/scores.json:198. The grouping is still wrong for the requested scaffold separation: two scaffold treatments of n=2 should each have null pass@3/pass^3. The other n≥3 group, fd6eb08…, is n=3, c=3 and yields both metrics 1. All four pypdf launch failures remain outside n.

Documentation: claim → artifact → disposition

Rows group repeated claims across README, architecture, grading and ops; a “verified” entry is limited to the artifact/code stated, not an external service's present health. Historical failures were compared with the ledger, available scenario validation files and saved job reports. External research/history claims lacking a local artifact are marked unsupported rather than inferred from their presence in prose.

Claim and location Artifact / code Verified / unsupported / false
Three registered valid scenarios; F2P/P2P 1/84, 6/3, 2/95. README.md:142 registry.json:1, corresponding scenario/compile/validation files; artifact summary Verified. All three registry/build/validation hashes agree in the snapshot.
Oracle 1, no-op 0, wrong 0, three tampers 0; per-control base/gold statuses. docs/grading.md:129 workspace/scenarios/mwaskom--seaborn-3190/validation.json:1, workspace/scenarios/scikit-learn--scikit-learn-13584/validation.json:1, workspace/scenarios/py-pdf--pypdf-3826/validation.json:1 Verified. seaborn registry still records befc959d…; validation 750e014c…. docs/grading.md:133 registry.json:1, workspace/scenarios/mwaskom--seaborn-3190/compile.json:1 False as current state: both point to cfa48d128c0f….

v1/v2 instruction and scaffold are distinct experimental changes. docs/grading.md:219 Frozen run builds, reports and ledger entries 128–145 Verified historical sequence; scaffold is not separated in one saved score group.

No stakeholder-v2 trials exist; earlier trials used v1. docs/grading.md:243 All 28 local transcripts and configs, plus three mirrored VM records Verified for the snapshot. Prompt-version string alone is insufficient provenance: default remains v1; review mode/build currently helps distinguish new configurations.
v2 never names unknown identifiers or chooses options; never sees code. docs/architecture.md:87 Prompt/filter/confirmation code False as an unconditional code guarantee. Finite term/marker filters and prompt rules; arbitrary confirmation content is accepted.
Author-only fact records excluded, request-body binding, locked freeze, persisted responses. docs/architecture.md:84 Stakeholder view/service/session and their tests Verified structurally. Three changes with the greatest effect on reward trust

  1. Make execution lineage immutable and shared: derive the complete effective run config once, bind probe jobs to measured inputs, and verify compiled output/base manifests before reuse. The concurrent helper change addresses the observed scaffold identity split; completing these checks also prevents stale measurements from being relabeled.
  2. Make task meaning reconstructible: record every removed span occurrence, reconstruct the brief in schema validation, require provenance for every visible requirement, and ensure negative controls change behavior independently of comments/docstrings. Validation should explain which behavior each control tests.
  3. Publish evidence that supports the reported claim: split historical scaffold groups, save per-instance judge predictions, generate tables from an explicit frozen inventory, preserve operational session evidence, and label prompt-only disclosure guarantees and in-process pytest limitations accurately. For a stronger reward boundary, trusted assertions must ultimately be isolated from submitted Python rather than relying solely on mutually consistent reports.
